text:
B: Alright. Craig.
A: Hello. Carys.
B: Gemma said you'd be the sensible one. Flooding, is it?
A: That's probably fair. Flood risk and drainage, yes. What did she say about you?
B: Nothing, I don't think. I'm an instrument tech at a water treatment works near Warrington.
A: Oh, right. So we're sort of in the same trade, just at different ends of the pipe.
B: Yeah, that's it. You stop it going everywhere, I check it's clean when it gets to us.
A: What do you do day to day?
B: Sensors, flow meters, control panels. Calibrate them, fix them when they go. I'm on call this week, so far it's been quiet. Touch wood. Last time I was on, a level sensor at a pump station kept alarming every night at three, and it turned out to be a spider nest in the housing.
A: That's brilliant. I mean, it's not, at three in the morning.
B: It wasn't brilliant at the time, no.
A: Flow data's half my life, to be fair. When the models don't match the gauges, it's usually a meter somewhere that nobody's looked at for years.
B: That'll be one of mine, probably.
A: I won't hold it against you.
B: Where are you based?
A: Mold, but the office is in Chester. The A55 roadworks are a nightmare at the minute.
B: The M6 round Warrington's no better. Every morning.
A: It's always the same bit, isn't it.
B: Always. We were in North Wales last summer, actually. Tenby, well, that's South, but we came back through. That's the photo behind me, our Ruby on the beach.
A: I did wonder. She looks like she's having a good time.
B: She'd have stayed all day. She's four. Starts reception in September. Gemma told me to get her doing her own coat and shoes.
A: Good advice. I remember that stage. Rhys is sixteen now, mocks coming up. Very relaxed about it.
B: Unlike you?
A: Unlike me. You've been talking to people.
B: Bit of a guess, that.
A: It's a good guess. Do you get out walking at all, or is it all callouts?
B: The Lakes a couple of times a year, and Pennington Flash with Ruby. Nothing big. You?
A: Moel Famau most weekends. I'm out early before the cloud comes in. And I swim before work.
B: Before work? That's commitment.
A: It's habit more than anything. If I stop, I won't start again.
B: That's me with five-a-side. I'm thirty-five, if I miss two weeks I'll never go back.
A: Yeah, no, I believe that.
B: That's about it really. Nice to meet someone who knows what a flow meter is.
